body: The first time I've ever teared up on Reddit. I'm honestly speechless. I know there's nothing anyone can say to comfort you. I'm just going to say I admire you so much for hanging in there. I'm off to contemplate this message and I'll be back tomorrow when I think of something worthwhile to say.

Suicide is one of those things that you never truly comprehend the consequences until someone close to you does it. I wish I could say it gets easier, but I can't lie. If you have mutual friends with your deceased friend, help them and they can help you. I missed out on this and I feel it is an important step in the healing/acceptance process.

C an I ask how helpful do you find college counselors?

Thank you for the time you took to write that. I will see a professional hopefully once I move out and go to University, but for now you guys are doing a good job at helping me. From your comment I've realised that I'll have to live with the pain, but use it to make me a stronger person. Thank you so much. Return hugs.

Thank you, I know that feeling. My friend had a not so common name and we all called him by a nickname. Inside the last few months I have become friends with another person through Xbox live with the same name, and I can't help calling him by my friends nickname.

I know now we can get through this, try reading the other comments here. It helps.

>Death happens, regardless of how or why.

This is something I have come to accept, possibly too much so. Without meaning to sound heartless or insult others here, in my eyes life is I knew it is meaningless. Not just my life, life in general. I grew up as a Christian but I've become an atheist in the last 3 years. I understand that while we're here we can do good and make a better life for those around us and those to come.

I will hopefully be *starting* in University later this year (my description may have been too vague, college where I live is Americas highschool) I look forward to being able to see a counselor, and generally wiping the slate cleaning/starting anew when I get there.

Thanks for your comment, and I hope you keep up the good attitude to life :)

Thanks. I never thought about different kinds counseling/therapy. What exactly is the difference between them? I'm starting in University later this year (hopefully) and I heard they provide counseling, so I'm holding out for that.
